title: Trace validation depth through an authorized boundary
description: Switch scenarios to see how the same entry point can produce a narrow exposure finding, a controlled validation, an approved internal path, or an immediate stop. Select any node to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Assessor
nodes.detail: Runs only reviewed actions, preserves timestamps and evidence, and stops when the engagement contract says to stop.

nodes.label: Scope gate
nodes.detail: Matches each target, identity, action, time window, and validation depth to the written rules of engagement before execution.

nodes.label: Public edge
nodes.detail: Represents an approved externally reachable service. Discovery evidence does not by itself prove exploitability or business impact.

nodes.label: Application
nodes.detail: Receives the least-impacting proof needed to confirm or reject the hypothesis under the selected role and state.

nodes.label: Internal zone
nodes.detail: May be reached only when the rules of engagement explicitly authorize the route, destination set, session type, and cleanup plan.

nodes.label: Evidence record
nodes.detail: Stores the claim, target, precondition, action, observed result, affected boundary, cleanup proof, and confidence without unnecessary sensitive data.

nodes.label: System owner
nodes.detail: Accepts or rejects the finding, owns remediation, confirms cleanup, and defines the evidence required for a retest.

scenarios.label: Exposure only
scenarios.summary: The objective is to identify a reachable service and preserve enough evidence for the owner to verify the exposure. No exploitation is needed.
scenarios.result: Report the exposed service, target, observation time, and supporting response. Do not inflate a reachability observation into a confirmed exploit or business-impact claim.

scenarios.label: Controlled validation
scenarios.summary: The approved objective requires a least-impacting application proof. The assessor records the precondition, exact request, observed behavior, and cleanup result.
scenarios.result: The evidence can support a confirmed application finding for this target and state. It does not authorize a pivot or access to unrelated records.

scenarios.label: Approved path
scenarios.summary: A multi-step objective explicitly permits a bounded path from the application into one named internal zone, with a session limit and cleanup contract.
scenarios.result: The result demonstrates one authorized attack path and the control assumptions it crossed. Stop at the named internal boundary and avoid treating one path as proof that the whole network is reachable.

scenarios.label: Stop at boundary
scenarios.summary: The application exposes a route toward an internal zone, but that destination and pivot action are outside the written scope.
scenarios.result: Stop before pivoting. Record the potential path as an unvalidated hypothesis, notify the engagement owner, and amend scope only through the agreed authorization process.
